blocks.text: Under Sampling addressed class imbalance by genuinely shrinking the majority class, at the real, permanent cost of discarding data. Over sampling takes the genuine opposite approach, growing the minority class instead, until it reaches a comparable count to the majority, keeping every single majority row fully intact throughout.

This topic covers exactly how over sampling duplicates minority class rows, the genuine, real advantage of never losing any majority class data, a different but equally real risk this technique introduces, exact duplicate rows that let a model simply memorize them rather than genuinely learn from them, and a direct comparison between this technique and under sampling real tradeoffs.
1. How Over Sampling Actually Works

blocks.alt: 100 minority rows get duplicated to match 900 majority rows

blocks.text: Over sampling genuinely duplicates rows from the minority class, repeatedly copying existing minority examples until that class count becomes comparable to the majority class. A dataset with 950 majority rows and 50 minority rows might genuinely become 950 and 950, after duplicating minority rows roughly 19 times over.

This is genuinely the direct mirror image of under sampling, instead of removing majority rows to shrink that class down, over sampling adds copies of minority rows to grow that class up, arriving at the exact same genuine goal, a balanced class distribution, from the opposite direction.
2. The Real, Genuine Advantage: No Data Loss

blocks.alt: Over sampling causes no data loss

blocks.text: Every genuine majority class row stays fully present in the resulting dataset, unlike under sampling, which genuinely, permanently discards a real portion of that class. This means no genuine majority class signal is ever lost, the model still sees the complete, real picture of what the majority class actually looks like.

This is a genuinely real, meaningful advantage over the previous topic, directly resolving the information loss concern that was under sampling most serious drawback, at the cost of a different, equally real tradeoff covered next.
3. A Worked Example

blocks.alt: 100 rows copied nine times each become 900 rows

blocks.text: Applying random over sampling with imbalanced-learn shows the genuine duplication directly, on the exact same small, imbalanced dataset used in the previous topic.

code.content:
from imblearn.over_sampling import RandomOverSampler
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({"amount": [50, 60, 45, 5000, 30, 70, 40, 6200]})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1])

sampler = RandomOverSampler(random_state=42)
X_resampled, y_resampled = sampler.fit_resample(X, y)

print(y_resampled.value_counts())
print(X_resampled)

blocks.text: The genuinely minority class, originally only 2 rows against 6 majority rows, gets grown up to match the majority class count exactly, and the printed X_resampled genuinely shows the same two original minority amounts, 5000 and 6200, appearing multiple times as exact, identical copies.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: After over sampling, genuinely check for exact duplicate rows in the resulting dataset. Seeing the same row repeated many times is expected here, but worth confirming directly rather than assuming.

blocks.text: 4. The Real Risk: Overfitting to Exact Duplicates

blocks.alt: Exact duplicate rows make the model overfit to them

blocks.text: An exact duplicate row genuinely carries no new information whatsoever, it is, quite literally, the identical data point seen again. A model trained on many exact copies of the same few minority examples can genuinely memorize those specific points directly, rather than learning the real, underlying pattern that would genuinely generalize to new, unseen minority examples.

This is a genuinely real, distinct risk from anything covered in under sampling, that topic risked losing real signal, this topic risks a model that appears to perform well specifically because it has memorized a small, repeated set of exact examples, not because it has genuinely learned to recognize the minority class in general.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Over sampling trades real data loss for a real overfitting risk. Neither cost disappears entirely, they simply take different forms, worth weighing directly against each other for any specific real project.

blocks.text: 5. A Concrete Picture of the Duplication

Visualizing one genuine original minority row being copied several times over makes the real mechanism, and its real cost, directly concrete, every one of those copies is genuinely, exactly identical, sharing the exact same feature values in every column.

A model encountering this repeated, identical pattern many times over during training can genuinely start treating that one specific row as disproportionately representative of the entire minority class, exactly the memorization risk covered above, made visually concrete here.
6. Comparing Under Sampling and Over Sampling Directly

blocks.alt: Under sampling removes rows while over sampling duplicates rows

blocks.text: These two techniques genuinely represent opposite strategies toward the exact same goal, class balance, and they carry genuinely different, real costs as a direct result. Under sampling real cost is losing majority class data permanently, over sampling real cost is a genuine overfitting risk from exact duplicate minority rows.

Neither technique is genuinely, universally superior, the right choice depends on the specific dataset at hand, how much majority data can genuinely be afforded to lose, and how severe the real overfitting risk from duplication is likely to be given how few minority examples actually exist.

blocks.text: 7. The Same Training Only Discipline Applies

blocks.alt: Over sampling happens on the train set only, never the test set

blocks.text: Exactly as with under sampling, over sampling should genuinely be applied only to the training set, never to validation or test. A validation or test set artificially balanced through duplication would genuinely misrepresent how the model actually performs on real, naturally imbalanced data, exactly the same leakage adjacent concern covered in the previous topic.

This discipline is genuinely worth restating clearly here, it is easy to assume a technique this simple carries no real leakage risk at all, but applying it beyond the training set genuinely undermines the honest evaluation every split in this course has been built to protect.

blocks.text: 8. Over Sampling Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Over sampling is covered here, SMOTE comes next

blocks.text: Under Sampling and Over Sampling together cover the two most direct, basic strategies for addressing class imbalance, remove from the majority or duplicate the minority, each carrying its own distinct, real cost. Neither, though, is genuinely the most sophisticated answer available.

The next topic, SMOTE, directly addresses over sampling exact duplicate weakness, generating genuinely new, synthetic minority examples instead of simply copying existing ones, offering a real, meaningful improvement worth understanding in detail.

items: Over sampling genuinely duplicates minority class rows until both classes reach a comparable count.
Unlike under sampling, it genuinely loses no majority class data at all.
Exact duplicate rows carry genuinely no new information, risking real overfitting through memorization.
Under sampling and over sampling represent genuinely opposite strategies with different real costs.
Over sampling must genuinely be applied only to the training set, exactly like under sampling.
The next topic, SMOTE, generates genuinely synthetic new minority examples instead of exact duplicates.
